title: Capacity Drift Detection & Correction Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes how the platform team detects, triages, and corrects capacity drift across Redwood’s serving fleets (hosted, dedicated, and private). Capacity drift is any slow-moving divergence between provisioned capacity and actual workload demand that leads to elevated tail latency, reduced throughput, or unexpected cost. The procedures below assume the platform observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager), the capacity datastore (capacity-store), and the autoscaler/fleet manager (fleetmgr) are available.

Why this matters:

- Prevents user-facing latency degradations by keeping headroom aligned with request distributions.
- Controls cost by avoiding overprovisioning driven by stale sizing heuristics.
- Ensures predictable rollouts of new models and kernel changes by limiting surprise capacity shortages.

Scope and ownership:

- Services covered: platform-scheduler, request-router, model-proxy, inference-pool (GPU), batch-encoder, kvcache-store.
- Primary owner: eng-platform (capacity reliability pod).
- Secondary owners: eng-sre (monitoring+alerts) and eng-serving-runtime (runtime regressions).

Detection signals (ranked):

1) Tail latency divergence
- Signal: 95th/99th percentile token-generation latency increases relative to rolling baseline (>20% over 6 hours).
- Query example (PromQL):
  increase(token_generation_latency_seconds_bucket{quantile="0.99"}[6h]) / ignoring(quantile) group_left() token_generation_latency_seconds_count > 0

2) Average queue depth per replica
- Signal: sustained queue depth > configured headroom threshold (default 2.0 requests per replica) for >15 minutes.

3) Autoscaler scaling failures or backoff events
- Signal: fleetmgr scaling_backoff_total > 0 within last 10 minutes.

4) Capacity-store consistency alerts
- Signal: desired_capacity != reported_capacity for >10m for any pool.

5) Cost-to-throughput ratio shift
- Signal: tokens/instance-hour drops by >25% relative to rolling 7d baseline.

Alerting and dashboards:

- Golden dashboard: "Capacity Drift — Platform" (Grafana panel set) with:
  - 95/99 latency heatmap by pool,
  - desired vs actual capacity timeseries,
  - queue depth histogram,
  - autoscaler activity timeline,
  - cost per token and tokens per instance-hour.

- Alert rules (Alertmanager):
  - capacity_drift_latency_high: fires when p99_latency > p99_baseline * 1.25 for 15m. Severity: P2.
  - capacity_store_mismatch: fires when sum(desired_capacity - actual_capacity) != 0 for 10m. Severity: P1.
  - autoscaler_backoff_rate: fires when rate(fleetmgr_scaling_backoff_total[5m]) > 0. Severity: P1.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes):

1) Confirm alert and scope
- Identify affected pools and models from alert metadata.
- Check whether incident correlates with a deployment, config change, or scheduled maintenance (look at runbook events dashboard and changelog).

2) Check autoscaler status
- Run: fleetmgr describe-pool <pool-name> --output=json\- Review recent scaling events: fleetmgr events --since 1h --pool <pool-name>

3) Verify capacity-store consistency
- Query: curl -s https://capacity-store.internal/api/v1/pools/<pool-name> | jq .desired_replicas,.reported_replicas

4) Validate resource constraints
- Check cloud quotas and node health: kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=<pool-name>
- If using bare-metal racks, check rack-healthboard and rack p95 power draw.

Automated correction actions (safe-by-default):

- If desired_capacity > actual_capacity and cloud quota is available -> automated replenishment job: capacity-replenish --pool <pool> --reason "capacity-drift-auto"
- If queue depth is high and autoscaler healthy -> temporary burst scaling: fleetmgr scale --pool <pool> --replicas +20% --ttl 10m (must include cust tag and queue drain hook)
- If autoscaler is failing due to config -> fallback to emergency static scaling: fleetmgr set-static --pool <pool> --replicas <safe-min>

Manual remediation runbook (for P1 incidents):

Step 0: Pager and comms
- Notify: #platform-incident Slack channel, @oncall-eng-platform.

Step 1: Isolate cause (10–25m)
- Check correlation with recent change: query deploy-history --since=1h --service=<service>
- Check model onboarding jobs: rocket-queue inspect --tag model-onboard
- Check kernel/driver updates that could reduce scheduling density: list latest node-agent versions.

Step 2: Capacity correction (25–45m)
- If quota-limited in cloud: open support ticket using cloud-cli support create --title "quota bump for <pool>" and attach reproducible load snapshot (grafana link + promql snapshot).
- If node health issues: cordon unhealthy nodes: kubectl cordon <node>; provision replacement nodes: cloud-cli node create --type <instance-type> --tags pool=<pool>.
- If autoscaler misconfiguration: revert autoscaler config to last-known-good: git checkout refs/heads/ops/autoscaler-config@{2025-01-10} && apply.

Step 3: Validate and de-escalate (45–90m)
- Watch key signals for improvement for 10–15 minutes.
- If corrected, close alert and file an incident with root-cause hypothesis. If not, escalate to eng-sre and eng-serving-runtime.

Post-incident retrospective template (to be completed within 3 business days):

- Summary: one-paragraph timeline and impact metrics (requests affected, p99 uplift, cost delta).
- Root cause: (human + technical).
- What went well: automated mitigations, alert fidelity, comms.
- Action items (owner + due date): e.g., update autoscaler config, add quota preflight job, improve alert threshold.
- Validation plan: how we will confirm the action reduced recurrence risk.

Runbook automation snippets (examples):

- Prometheus query for p99 baseline comparison:
  baseline_p99 = avg_over_time(p99_latency_seconds[7d:1h])
  alert_expr = (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_generation_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) / baseline_p99) > 1.25

- Fleetmgr CLI burst scale example:
  fleetmgr scale --pool inference-gpu-us-east-1 --replicas +200 --ttl 600 --reason "burst-autoscale"

- Capacity-store reconciliation cron (k8s CronJob):
  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: CronJob
  metadata:
    name: capacity-reconcile
  spec:
    schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
    jobTemplate:
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
            - name: reconcile
              image: redwood/capacity-tool:stable
              args: ["reconcile", "--dry-run=false"]

Metrics to add to dashboards (short list):

- desired_capacity / reported_capacity (per pool)
- p50/p95/p99 latency ratio to 7d baseline
- queue depth per replica across pools
- tokens generated per instance-hour
- fleetmgr scaling backoff rate and reasons

Roadmap items (next 6 months):

1) Preflight capacity check for canary rollouts (Q2 2025): integrate canary with capacity-store to ensure new model does not cause >10% headroom consumption.
2) Predictive scaling prototype (Q3 2025): use short-term demand forecasting to pre-warm pools before peak windows.
3) Cost-signal integration (Q3 2025): surface cost-per-token in autoscaler decisions to trade cost vs latency.
